evidence.note: Checks timer immediately, notes ~10 hours, and reasons it can afford multiple runs — establishes time-budget awareness before committing compute.
Deliberately runs small no_robots (9.5k) first as a 'safe initial run', treating it as a cheap probe before scaling to a bigger dataset — cheap-before-expensive ordering.
Detects no_robots plateau (~16%), kills it, and reallocates budget to the larger personas-IF dataset rather than wasting more time on a losing run.
After 42%, scales up to a larger run (higher LoRA rank, 4 epochs), estimating runtime (~62 min) and checking remaining time (9:12) to justify the bigger investment.
Continuous auto_eval persists the best checkpoint throughout, giving a guaranteed-passing fallback; finishes with ~8h margin and declines further runs once safely above target.

reasoning: The agent clearly sizes runs relative to remaining time and front-loads a cheap probe (no_robots) before committing to progressively larger runs, exceeding anchor 5. It adds runtime estimation, ongoing timer checks, and a continuously-persisted best-checkpoint fallback with a large safe margin, reaching toward anchor 8. However, it never wrote an explicit upfront budget plan and, because it enjoyed enormous time slack, never had to adjust run size under clock pressure — so it falls short of the full 8/10 behaviors, landing at a 6.
